scope: Theorem 7.1 of the manuscript “Fontaine–Mazur modularity at the prime 2” (preprints/Fontaine-Mazur-modularity-at-the-prime-2-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 010 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3c8797c7d468cdcc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 53. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let r satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1 and be not virtually solvable. Then r is pro-modular over some solvable totally real Galois extension of Q, of even degree and split completely at 2. More generally, fix a complete integral framed deformation family over Q, with determinant χ = det r, containing the coefficient point defined by r, and with ramification confined to a finite set. The closed trace image of this family is pro-modular after restriction to one common extension of the stated kind, at one fixed tame level.
